//: NodeNext, not Bundler. The emitted JavaScript has to resolve under plain
Node — `demo-backend` compiles against this package with NodeNext and its
tests run in Node — as well as inside every example app's Vite build. That
is why every relative import in `src/` carries an explicit `.js`
extension: it is the one import form both resolvers agree on.
`composite` is what lets `demo-backend` name this project as a reference
and have `tsc -b` build it first. See demo-backend/tsconfig.json.
`declarationMap` and `sourceMap` are OFF because `files` in package.json
ships `dist` without `src`. A map that names sources the tarball does not
carry is a dead end in every consumer's debugger, so the honest build is
one with no maps rather than one with broken ones. Turn both on again, and
add `src` to `files`, if the sources are ever shipped alongside.
`tsBuildInfoFile` lives OUTSIDE `dist` so the incremental cache — a local
build artefact naming absolute paths on the machine that built it — cannot
be swept into the published tarball. `files` is an allow-list, so a file
at the package root is outside it by construction.
